items.title: Agency, interests, and social formation: CR-01A
items.rationale: Objective interests attributed from a position versus the person's account of their interests. Agreement does not establish that economic position determines every belief, or that the respondent supports a particular class politics.
items.interpretation_limits: “Interests” may mean material welfare, identity, rights, or preferences. CR-01C's examples can elicit simple agreement that education influences people; retain it only if the explanation distinguishes formation of goals from assistance in pursuing them. CR-01A may be heard as permission to dismiss other people's views, while CR-01B may be heard as courtesy rather than a claim about explanation. Vietnamese *lợi ích*, *lập trường*, and *thiết chế* need paraphrase testing. These items are demanding candidates for interviews, not introductory warm-up questions.

en.text: A person's economic position is usually a better guide to their political interests than the goals they say they have.

vi.text: Vị trí kinh tế của một người thường là căn cứ tốt hơn để hiểu lợi ích chính trị của họ so với những mục tiêu mà chính họ nói mình theo đuổi.

outcomes.title: How political interests and goals are explained
outcomes.intended_interpretation: Describe the separate weight a respondent gives to interests attributed from economic position, people's own reasons, and institutions that help form goals.
outcomes.evidence_required: Responses to CR-01A/B/C plus paraphrases distinguishing interests, goals, explanations and social influence. Ask which society or example grounds the judgment.
outcomes.unsupported_inferences: The cluster does not directly test the ability to dissent, measure agency or establish an individualist/collectivist identity. First-person explanations and social formation can both matter.

items.title: Agency, interests, and social formation: CR-01B
items.rationale: First-person reasons as explanations versus explanation by social location. Disagreement might concern rationalization, limited self-knowledge, or unreliable reporting; it does not establish that agency is unreal.
items.interpretation_limits: “Interests” may mean material welfare, identity, rights, or preferences. CR-01C's examples can elicit simple agreement that education influences people; retain it only if the explanation distinguishes formation of goals from assistance in pursuing them. CR-01A may be heard as permission to dismiss other people's views, while CR-01B may be heard as courtesy rather than a claim about explanation. Vietnamese *lợi ích*, *lập trường*, and *thiết chế* need paraphrase testing. These items are demanding candidates for interviews, not introductory warm-up questions.

en.text: Political commitments are best explained by the reasons people give, even when their group memberships suggest a different explanation.

items.title: Agency, interests, and social formation: CR-01C
items.rationale: Institutions as producers of goals versus instruments for prior goals. Agreement does not identify which institutions matter or deny that people can change them.
items.interpretation_limits: “Interests” may mean material welfare, identity, rights, or preferences. CR-01C's examples can elicit simple agreement that education influences people; retain it only if the explanation distinguishes formation of goals from assistance in pursuing them. en.text: Institutions such as schools and workplaces help form people's political goals, rather than simply responding to goals people already have.

items.title: Economic power, organized groups, and the state: CR-02A
items.rationale: Durable power beyond formal electoral participation. Agreement does not establish that every business owner acts together, or that abolishing private ownership is the desired remedy.
items.interpretation_limits: Country-specific beliefs can dominate this cluster. “Several groups” may mean fractions of the same class; “independently” may mean complete isolation rather than a partly autonomous power base. CR-02C's possibility wording may attract broad assent; keep it only if interviews show that the autonomy distinction adds information beyond CR-02A/B. These are causal beliefs, not a test of whether respondents prefer inequality.

en.text: When elections are competitive, control of major businesses still gives owners political power that ordinary voting cannot offset.

vi.text: Ngay cả khi bầu cử có sự cạnh tranh, quyền kiểm soát các doanh nghiệp lớn vẫn đem lại cho chủ sở hữu quyền lực chính trị mà việc bỏ phiếu thông thường không thể cân bằng được.

outcomes.title: Sources and persistence of political power
outcomes.intended_interpretation: Describe beliefs about business ownership beyond voting, bargaining among groups, and public officials' capacity to develop an independent power base.
outcomes.evidence_required: Responses to CR-02A/B/C with examples of mechanisms and clarification of whether the claim concerns a possible state, most states or a specific society.
outcomes.unsupported_inferences: Explanatory beliefs do not indicate approval of inequality, denial of elections, support for authoritarian government or membership in a class-based political tradition.

items.title: Economic power, organized groups, and the state: CR-02B
items.rationale: Negotiated plural influence versus predominant class rule. Agreement does not establish that bargaining power is equal, fair, or open to everyone.

en.text: The main direction of public policy usually reflects bargaining among several groups rather than the rule of one economic class.

items.rationale: State autonomy from owners of capital. Agreement does not show approval of bureaucracy, support for authoritarian rule, or rejection of class explanations in other cases.

items.title: What makes a choice free?: CR-03A
items.rationale: Voluntary acceptance under constrained alternatives. Agreement does not establish that the wage is fair, the contract is legitimate in every respect, or the employer owes no duties.
items.interpretation_limits: Respondents may silently assume savings, family support, or an abusive employer. CR-03C explicitly removes effective appeal, but still needs a distinction between a polite explanation and a remedy that can constrain the employer. Vietnamese *khiếu nại hữu hiệu* needs a plain-language paraphrase test. If answers depend mainly on an unstated fact, move the distinction into a specified scenario. Do not calculate a freedom continuum from the three responses.

en.text: An adult who accepts a job without being threatened has made a free choice, even when no other employer is hiring.

vi.text: Một người trưởng thành nhận một công việc mà không bị đe dọa đã đưa ra một lựa chọn tự do, ngay cả khi không có nơi nào khác đang tuyển dụng.

outcomes.title: Different meanings of freedom
outcomes.intended_interpretation: Describe whether the respondent counts unthreatened agreement, secure means to meet needs and protection from unreviewable dismissal as aspects of freedom.
outcomes.evidence_required: Responses to CR-03A/B/C and probes about alternatives, resources, standing power and effective appeal. Keep each proposition separate.
outcomes.unsupported_inferences: The three responses do not form a validated freedom continuum. A judgment that an action is free does not establish that it is fair; concern about domination does not identify a preferred ownership system.

items.title: What makes a choice free?: CR-03B
items.rationale: Material conditions as part of freedom. Agreement does not identify the institution that should secure those conditions, or imply support for any particular benefit program.
items.interpretation_limits: Respondents may silently assume savings, family support, or an abusive employer. en.text: Having no secure way to meet basic needs makes a person less free, even when no law blocks their choices.

items.rationale: A standing capacity to exercise power versus actual interference. Agreement does not establish opposition to all dismissals, management authority, or private employment.
items.interpretation_limits: Respondents may silently assume savings, family support, or an abusive employer. en.text: If workers have no effective way to appeal dismissal, their employer's power to dismiss them reduces their freedom even when that power is never used.

items.title: Desert, need, and particular obligations: CR-04A
items.rationale: Equal formal rules as a sufficient basis for deserved earnings despite unequal starting resources. Agreement does not establish opposition to taxes, support for every existing law, or a belief that effort alone causes income.
items.interpretation_limits: CR-04A bridges a claim about rules with a moral conclusion; respondents may reject the fairness of the imagined rules rather than the sufficiency claim. CR-04B can mean equal money or equal effective support. CR-04C concerns an individual's obligations and should not be generalized to a state's duties. Vietnamese *xứng đáng*, *đóng góp*, and *nghĩa vụ* require particular attention.

en.text: When the same legal rules apply to everyone, people deserve the income they earn even if they start with very different family resources.

vi.text: Khi mọi người đều chịu cùng những quy tắc pháp luật, họ xứng đáng được hưởng khoản thu nhập mình kiếm được, ngay cả khi xuất phát điểm về nguồn lực gia đình rất khác nhau.

outcomes.title: Desert, need and care-based obligation
outcomes.intended_interpretation: Distinguish judgments about deserved earnings under equal formal rules, public support based on need rather than contribution, and stronger personal duties within care relationships.
outcomes.evidence_required: Responses to CR-04A/B/C with clarification of contribution, effective support, deserving versus legal entitlement and the difference between a person's duty and a public official's mandate.
outcomes.unsupported_inferences: A person's care duties cannot be generalized to a state's obligations. The cluster is not a generosity score, compassion test or complete theory of distributive justice.

items.interpretation_limits: CR-04A bridges a claim about rules with a moral conclusion; respondents may reject the fairness of the imagined rules rather than the sufficiency claim. items.rationale: Relationship-based obligations relative to impartial need. Agreement does not imply that caring duties are unlimited, naturally assigned to women, or exclusively private.

items.title: Who should govern an enterprise?: CR-05A
items.rationale: Non-working ownership as a basis of final authority. The stated ownership arrangement keeps owners and workers distinct in this case without assuming that all enterprises are organized this way. Agreement does not establish support for unlimited authority, exemption from law, or the claim that investors alone bear risks.
items.interpretation_limits: “Enterprise,” “governing body,” and “essential service” need concrete paraphrases; different legal systems make different models familiar. Expected competence or investment flight may drive answers even when the stem asks about rightful authority. Record those causal expectations separately. A cooperative must not automatically be treated as a midpoint between public and private provision.

en.text: In an enterprise owned by people who do not work there, those owners should have final authority over its main decisions, even when workers oppose them.

vi.text: Trong một doanh nghiệp do những người không làm việc tại đó sở hữu, các chủ sở hữu này nên có quyền quyết định cuối cùng về những vấn đề chủ chốt, ngay cả khi người lao động phản đối.

outcomes.title: Claims to govern economic enterprises
outcomes.intended_interpretation: Describe the decision rights a respondent supports for non-working owners, workers and essential-service users.

items.title: Statistical evidence, experience, and dispersed knowledge: CR-06A
items.rationale: A default evidential priority when sources conflict. Agreement does not establish blind trust in statistics; disagreement may mean insufficient information about either source rather than rejection of research.

CR-06A could mostly measure trust in a familiar authority, CR-06B recognition or courtesy, and CR-06C views about an imagined planning technology. items.title: Membership, duties, and collective self-rule: CR-08A

items.title: Religion and public justification: CR-09A
items.rationale: Religious teaching as sufficient public justification. Agreement does not establish support for every religious interpretation, preference for a particular religion, or a claim that religious authority should directly govern.
items.interpretation_limits: CR-09A and CR-09B can both be endorsed if “justified” means morally justified in one but publicly authorized in the other. items.title: Inherited status, repair, and representation: CR-10A
items.rationale: Individual need versus inherited group membership as the eligibility basis for remedial assistance in a specified system of social closure. Agreement does not establish opposition to recording discrimination, denial of its history, or a general prohibition on every use of group identity.
items.interpretation_limits: CR-10A defines a fictional inherited hierarchy rather than equating caste, class, and race. It still abstracts from distinct histories and does not represent anti-caste thought adequately on its own. Respondents may reasonably combine need with group membership; record that position rather than forcing it into a false binary. “Earlier exclusion” in CR-10B may be too abstract without an example. Group labels can also freeze disputed identities. Dedicated anti-caste, Black, and other affected-community scholarship and review are needed before any coverage claim.

en.text: Imagine a society where birth assigns people to ranked groups that restrict marriage and job opportunities. Public assistance to remedy this discrimination should be based on individual need rather than inherited group membership.

vi.text: Hãy hình dung một xã hội nơi con người được xếp vào các nhóm có thứ bậc ngay từ khi sinh ra, với những hạn chế về kết hôn và việc làm theo nhóm. Hỗ trợ công nhằm khắc phục sự phân biệt đối xử này nên dựa trên nhu cầu của từng cá nhân thay vì việc một người thuộc nhóm nào từ khi sinh ra.

items.title: Inherited status, repair, and representation: CR-10C
items.rationale: Guaranteed group representation beyond formally open elections. Agreement does not establish who selects representatives, how groups are defined, or whether reserved seats should be permanent.
items.interpretation_limits: CR-10A defines a fictional inherited hierarchy rather than equating caste, class, and race. It still abstracts from distinct histories and does not represent anti-caste thought adequately on its own. Respondents may reasonably combine need with group membership; record that position rather than forcing it into a false binary. “Earlier exclusion” in CR-10B may be too abstract without an example. Group labels can also freeze disputed identities. Dedicated anti-caste, Black, and other affected-community scholarship and review are needed before any coverage claim.

en.text: People from groups kept out of decision-making should have guaranteed seats in public bodies, even when ordinary elections are open to everyone.

items.title: Ecological standing and limits: CR-11A
items.rationale: Non-instrumental ecological standing. Agreement does not establish equal moral standing for every organism or a rule for every conflict with human needs.
items.interpretation_limits: CR-11A and CR-11B use possibility rather than a general priority, which can yield easy agreement; their initial purpose is to locate a reason that needs a concrete follow-up. “Net public benefits” may be read as money alone or as an aggregate already including ecological value. If the latter makes CR-11C circular, replace the term in a scenario with specified benefits and ecological consequences. Do not infer positions on economic growth from these three responses alone.

en.text: Protecting a living ecosystem can be a political duty even when doing so brings no benefit to people.

outcomes.title: Ecological standing and limits on tradeoffs

outcomes.unsupported_inferences: These responses do not establish a position on all economic growth, equal sacrifice by all households, a specific environmental policy or an Indigenous political identity.

items.title: Consent, performance, and compulsory coordination: CR-12A
items.rationale: Revocable authorization relative to competence. Agreement does not establish a preference for direct democracy, a right to veto every decision, or agreement on who counts among those subject to a power.
items.interpretation_limits: “Right to rule” must be distinguished from legal power and ability to keep order; the Vietnamese draft uses *quyền chính đáng* to make legitimacy explicit. CR-12A may be read as elections alone, although other revocation procedures are possible. CR-12C bridges a moral preference for voluntary coordination with empirical expectations about its feasibility. No single response establishes a person's regime preference across all circumstances.

en.text: Even competent leaders should have only powers that those subject to them can regularly withdraw.

outcomes.unsupported_inferences: No single response establishes an authoritarian personality, acceptance of repression, a preferred regime in every circumstance or a complete anarchist/libertarian identity.

items.title: Disability, independence, and effective access: CR-13A

WCAG documents limits of web conformance only; it does not settle the normative content of CR-13D or obligations in every public service. Vietnamese translations are author drafts.

items.title: Household authority, unpaid care, and gendered roles: CR-14A
items.rationale: Voluntary agreement and a secure exit as sufficient grounds of fairness despite unequal tasks. This adds conditions of household consent to CR-04's duties to dependents.
items.interpretation_limits: These four stems do not cover gender or sexuality comprehensively. Money, free agreement, care, and a secure exit need concrete paraphrase tests. A formally available exit can still be costly; unequal earnings do not prove coercion. CR-14D intentionally raises a contested inference and does not assert that biology or social institutions alone explain gender. Independent feminist, queer, disability, and affected-reader review remains necessary. Mill's historical arguments are not a proxy for contemporary feminism; Pateman remains a reading proposal.

en.text: When adults have secure ways to live separately, a division of paid work and unpaid care that they freely agree is fair, even if one person does nearly all the care.

items.title: Emergency authority, renewal, and local discretion: CR-15A

items.interpretation_limits: Emergency wording can invite the reader to imagine war, disease, crime, or disaster with very different stakes. items.title: Data consent, collective effects, and decision authority: CR-16A
items.rationale: Whether permission from the data contributor is sufficient when inference reaches non-contributors. This concerns the reach of authorization, not whether consent is unnecessary or whether every inference is harmful.
items.interpretation_limits: Data may evoke surveillance, a harmless count, commercial profiling, or medical research. Accuracy does not establish fairness, legitimate purpose, or an effective remedy. Human review may be imagined as careful reconsideration or a rubber stamp. The propositions do not test technical literacy or infer support for censorship. W3C Privacy Principles describe normative web-governance concerns; they neither validate these items nor establish the efficacy of any offered institution.

en.text: An adult's informed permission is enough to authorize use of their data, even when patterns inferred from it influence decisions about people who did not share data.

outcomes.title: Consent, collective effects, and governance of data-based decisions
outcomes.intended_interpretation: Describe separately the reach assigned to individual permission, affected-public decision rights, human reconsideration under fixed eligibility rules, and purpose-bound public-interest use without universal permission. Preserve which source of authorization or remedy is being endorsed.
outcomes.evidence_required: Individual CR-16A/B/C/D responses and probes distinguishing a contributor from an affected person, prediction from legitimate allocation, consultation from binding authority, and review from a guarantee of favorable treatment. Independent content and bilingual comprehension review remain required.
outcomes.unsupported_inferences: No privacy-versus-progress score, technology competence estimate, view about every use of AI, political ideology, or endorsement of a real data program follows. The normative source principles are not validation evidence, and technical accuracy does not demonstrate fairness or consent.

items.title: Authority over shared resources and membership within self-government: CR-17A
items.rationale: A claim grounded in maintaining a shared institution, rather than a prediction that local decisions maximize output. Routine use and agreed downstream protections bound the proposed authority.
items.interpretation_limits: A generic water commons is not an Indigenous sovereignty measure or a proxy for any particular people. Resource ownership, customary authority, historical dispossession and citizenship are different claims. Readers may imagine absolute control, different legal rights, downstream emergencies or unequal competence that the text does not state. Vietnamese terms for established users and a binding say require paraphrase review. Source proposals and affected-community review remain incomplete.

en.text: A community that has maintained a shared water system should have final authority over its routine use, within agreed protections for people downstream.

outcomes.unsupported_inferences: No self-rule score, sovereignty diagnosis, Indigenous-identity inference, ethnic preference or ranking of local and national political cultures. Agreement with multiple propositions can be coherent.

items.interpretation_limits: These are difficult philosophical distinctions, not a left–right scale. items.interpretation_limits: Words such as reliable, explanation, knowledge, and important may carry different thresholds across readers. items.title: How to investigate public problems: comparison, meaning, history and participation: CR-23A
items.rationale: A default preference for comparative evidence when making a causal claim, not a claim that comparison alone proves causation or that accounts are useless.
items.interpretation_limits: A methods question can become a school test if one plan alone meets a specified mandate. Here the purpose is deliberately broader than causal estimation. CR-23C uses a strong completeness claim to expose views about historical explanation; it is not a claim that every study needs an unlimited history. items.title: Who can change the housing rules?
items.rationale:
Candidate reason labels for later review: ability to leave an unwanted relationship / `khả năng rời một quan hệ mình không muốn`; shared authority over common rules / `quyền cùng quyết định quy tắc chung`; protection when an individual loses a majority vote / `bảo vệ cá nhân khi họ thuộc phía thiểu số trong biểu quyết`; quickest useful help / `hỗ trợ có ích nhanh nhất`; confidence that the mechanism will work / `tin rằng cơ chế sẽ hoạt động`; other reason / `lý do khác`.

Do not enforce option/reason pairing. A respondent might choose A because ten households have urgent needs, because competing housing providers discipline managers, or because they distrust representation. B might express republican contestation, collective self-government, conservative stewardship of a shared place, or simple expectations of better rules. C might protect minorities, limit all officeholders, or minimize meeting burdens. None uniquely identifies a tradition.
items.interpretation_limits:
Distinguish the ability to leave a relationship, collective control over its rules, and an individual right to contest power. Keep municipal ownership fixed so that collective voice cannot be read simply as public-ownership preference. This concerns ordinary lawful rules, not permission to remove basic tenant rights.

This tests sensitivity to exercised interference while the capacity to interfere is constant. Changed answers could also reflect inferred trustworthiness or urgency; they do not establish an individual causal estimate or a definitive non-domination belief. Ask whether the participant imagined unstated misconduct.

Which decisions can you personally make? Does lawful mean reasonable? Does a resident board necessarily speak for you? What happens to the 110 households without a moving grant? What did “independent” mean to you? In Vietnamese, check whether `người xem xét` sounds like a mediator who lacks binding authority; the reversal power must remain explicit.

en.text:
**Your surroundings.** You live in a municipal housing estate with 120 households in a large city in your assigned fictional country. The estate manager can change rules about courtyard opening hours, visitors, and use of the meeting room after giving 30 days' notice. In the past year the manager has used that power twice. The existing rules are lawful. Residents disagree about whether those rules are reasonable.

**Your role.** You are an ordinary resident answering a consultation. You can recommend a package; you cannot spend the budget, appoint officials, or impose a rule. The municipal council will decide.

**What is fixed.** The council has set aside 90,000 credits for one two-year package. Municipal ownership, rent levels, repair duties, protection from eviction, and existing legal rights remain the same under every package. All packages have approved funding and can operate for the full two years. Ten suitable homes at the same rent are available elsewhere for households that want to move; there is no promise of further vacancies.

**Which package would you recommend?**

| Option | What the package does | What it gives up |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A — Make leaving affordable | Fund moving expenses of 9,000 credits for each of ten households that wish to leave. If more than ten apply, allocate the grants by lottery. The manager keeps the present rule-making power. | Households that stay gain no additional control over those rules; only ten households receive moving support. |
| B — Give residents a collective decision | Fund accessible elections, meeting support, and independent advice for a resident board. A new rule about the three listed subjects needs the board's approval. Urgent safety repairs remain outside its veto. | Seeking agreement can delay ordinary rule changes by up to 60 days, and an individual resident can still lose a board vote. |
| C — Give each resident a way to challenge a rule | Fund an independent reviewer and free help with submissions. Any resident may challenge a rule as unreasonable. The reviewer can reverse it, with a decision due within 15 working days. Funding covers all eligible complaints. | A rule can operate while a case is heard; residents gain no collective vote over the manager's future proposals. |

You may also answer “uncertain,” “none of these represents my decision,” or “skip.” All three packages remain lawful in this fictional setting.

vi.text:
**Bối cảnh của bạn.** Bạn sống tại một khu nhà ở thuộc sở hữu của thành phố, gồm 120 hộ, trong một đô thị lớn của quốc gia giả định được giao. Sau khi thông báo trước 30 ngày, người quản lý khu nhà có thể thay đổi quy định về giờ mở sân chung, khách đến thăm và việc sử dụng phòng sinh hoạt chung. Trong năm qua, người quản lý đã sử dụng quyền này hai lần. Các quy định hiện hành đều hợp pháp. Cư dân có ý kiến khác nhau về việc các quy định đó có hợp lý hay không.

**Vai trò của bạn.** Bạn là một cư dân bình thường, đang góp ý trong đợt tham vấn. Bạn có thể đề xuất một phương án; bạn không có quyền chi ngân sách, bổ nhiệm người phụ trách hoặc ban hành quy định. Hội đồng thành phố sẽ quyết định.

**Những điều được giữ nguyên.** Hội đồng đã dành 90.000 đơn vị tiền giả định cho một phương án kéo dài hai năm. Trong cả ba phương án, quyền sở hữu của thành phố, mức thuê, nghĩa vụ sửa chữa, quy định bảo vệ người thuê khỏi việc bị buộc rời nhà và các quyền pháp lý hiện có đều không thay đổi. Mọi phương án đã được duyệt kinh phí và có thể hoạt động đủ hai năm. Ở nơi khác có mười căn nhà phù hợp với mức thuê bằng hiện tại, dành cho những hộ muốn chuyển đi; không có cam kết sẽ có thêm nhà trống.

**Bạn sẽ đề xuất phương án nào?**

| Phương án | Nội dung | Điều phải đánh đổi |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A — Hỗ trợ để có thể chuyển đi | Chi 9.000 đơn vị tiền hỗ trợ chuyển nhà cho mỗi hộ trong số mười hộ muốn rời khu nhà. Nếu có hơn mười hộ đăng ký, các suất hỗ trợ được phân bổ bằng bốc thăm. Người quản lý giữ quyền đặt quy định như hiện nay. | Các hộ ở lại không có thêm quyền kiểm soát những quy định này; chỉ mười hộ được hỗ trợ chuyển nhà. |
| B — Để cư dân cùng quyết định | Chi cho việc tổ chức bầu cử mà cư dân có thể tham gia, hỗ trợ họp và tư vấn độc lập cho ban đại diện cư dân. Một quy định mới về ba vấn đề đã nêu phải được ban đại diện đồng ý. Ban không có quyền ngăn việc sửa chữa khẩn cấp để bảo đảm an toàn. | Việc tìm sự đồng thuận có thể làm chậm thay đổi quy định thông thường tối đa 60 ngày; một cư dân vẫn có thể thua trong cuộc biểu quyết của ban. |
| C — Cho từng cư dân quyền yêu cầu xem xét quy định | Chi cho một người xem xét độc lập và hỗ trợ miễn phí khi nộp yêu cầu. Bất kỳ cư dân nào cũng có thể đề nghị xem xét một quy định mà họ cho là không hợp lý. Người xem xét có quyền hủy quy định đó và phải quyết định trong 15 ngày làm việc. Kinh phí đủ xử lý mọi yêu cầu đủ điều kiện. | Quy định có thể vẫn được áp dụng trong thời gian xem xét; cư dân không có thêm quyền biểu quyết tập thể đối với các đề xuất sau này của người quản lý. |

Bạn cũng có thể chọn “chưa chắc,” “không phương án nào thể hiện quyết định của tôi,” hoặc “bỏ qua.” Trong bối cảnh giả định này, cả ba phương án đều hợp pháp.

en.label: Make leaving affordable
en.description: Fund moving expenses of 9,000 credits for each of ten households that wish to leave. If more than ten apply, allocate the grants by lottery. The manager keeps the present rule-making power.
en.tradeoff: Households that stay gain no additional control over those rules; only ten households receive moving support.

vi.label: Hỗ trợ để có thể chuyển đi
vi.description: Chi 9.000 đơn vị tiền hỗ trợ chuyển nhà cho mỗi hộ trong số mười hộ muốn rời khu nhà. Nếu có hơn mười hộ đăng ký, các suất hỗ trợ được phân bổ bằng bốc thăm. Người quản lý giữ quyền đặt quy định như hiện nay.
vi.tradeoff: Các hộ ở lại không có thêm quyền kiểm soát những quy định này; chỉ mười hộ được hỗ trợ chuyển nhà.

en.label: Give residents a collective decision
en.description: Fund accessible elections, meeting support, and independent advice for a resident board. A new rule about the three listed subjects needs the board's approval. Urgent safety repairs remain outside its veto.
en.tradeoff: Seeking agreement can delay ordinary rule changes by up to 60 days, and an individual resident can still lose a board vote.

vi.label: Để cư dân cùng quyết định
vi.description: Chi cho việc tổ chức bầu cử mà cư dân có thể tham gia, hỗ trợ họp và tư vấn độc lập cho ban đại diện cư dân. Một quy định mới về ba vấn đề đã nêu phải được ban đại diện đồng ý. Ban không có quyền ngăn việc sửa chữa khẩn cấp để bảo đảm an toàn.
vi.tradeoff: Việc tìm sự đồng thuận có thể làm chậm thay đổi quy định thông thường tối đa 60 ngày; một cư dân vẫn có thể thua trong cuộc biểu quyết của ban.

en.label: Give each resident a way to challenge a rule
en.description: Fund an independent reviewer and free help with submissions. Any resident may challenge a rule as unreasonable. The reviewer can reverse it, with a decision due within 15 working days. Funding covers all eligible complaints.
en.tradeoff: A rule can operate while a case is heard; residents gain no collective vote over the manager's future proposals.

vi.label: Cho từng cư dân quyền yêu cầu xem xét quy định
vi.description: Chi cho một người xem xét độc lập và hỗ trợ miễn phí khi nộp yêu cầu. Bất kỳ cư dân nào cũng có thể đề nghị xem xét một quy định mà họ cho là không hợp lý. Người xem xét có quyền hủy quy định đó và phải quyết định trong 15 ngày làm việc. Kinh phí đủ xử lý mọi yêu cầu đủ điều kiện.
vi.tradeoff: Quy định có thể vẫn được áp dụng trong thời gian xem xét; cư dân không có thêm quyền biểu quyết tập thể đối với các đề xuất sau này của người quản lý.

outcomes.title: Housing governance: exit, voice and individual appeal
outcomes.intended_interpretation: Describe the consultation package favored when municipal ownership is fixed and residents can gain moving assistance, collective rule approval or individual review. Retain the reason separately.
outcomes.evidence_required: The CR-S01 action, its stated reason, understood consultation authority and the exact base or variant facts shown. The variant needs a planned design before estimating an effect.
outcomes.unsupported_inferences: A moving grant does not necessarily indicate market ideology; collective voice and individual appeal do not uniquely identify traditions. Choice changes cannot identify a causal role effect or a definitive belief about non-domination.

items.title: Who receives the extra respite hours?
items.rationale:
Candidate reason labels: greatest unmet recipient need / `nhu cầu chưa được đáp ứng cao nhất của người được chăm sóc`; sustaining an unpaid caring relationship / `duy trì quan hệ chăm sóc không hưởng lương`; carers' claims to rest as persons in their own right / `quyền được nghỉ của người chăm sóc với tư cách một cá nhân`; equal shares of additional public support / `phần hỗ trợ công bổ sung bằng nhau`; reducing reliance on contested priority rankings / `giảm sự phụ thuộc vào cách xếp ưu tiên còn gây tranh luận`; responsibility for a voluntarily accepted role / `trách nhiệm đối với vai trò đã tự nguyện nhận`; other reason / `lý do khác`.

A could express recipient-centered capability, triage, or a narrow interpretation of the officer's duty. B could express care ethics, distributive concern for carers, or a consequentialist prediction that exhausted carers will stop providing care. C could express equal standing, skepticism about measurement, or an implementable rule. A respondent could favor B while holding a strongly family-centered worldview. A respondent could favor A while supporting extensive public care overall.
items.interpretation_limits:
Separate attention to the care recipient, attention to the caring relationship, and equal additional provision. All options use the same public care service; no response is scored as public/private preference or as a measure of compassion.

The assignment describes the past; it does not create a present legal or family power to compel care. This is a proposed contrast about the history of consent, not a claim that consent history is independent of all real-world consequences. Probe whether the respondent changed the stipulated current willingness or imagined coercion continuing now. If the variant is understood as changing present coercion or family safety, revise it or drop the contrast.

Who receives the service and who gains rest? Are the two priority groups the same twenty households? Does equal increase mean equal total need is met? Did you assume that carers are all women, family members, or unemployed? Does the Vietnamese wording convey temporary replacement of care, rather than stopping care or paying the carer? Ask participants to reconstruct the 20/20/10 overlap; use a simple card diagram if the numbers otherwise dominate the interview.

en.text:
**Your surroundings.** You administer a respite-care service in a rural district of your assigned fictional country. Forty separate households receive the service; in this exercise, each has one adult care recipient and one main unpaid carer. Some carers are relatives and some are friends. Every care recipient already receives the same two hours of weekly respite support. Other funded services meet immediate safety needs under every package below.

**Your role.** You are a non-elected service officer with written authority to select one of the three approved allocation rules for the next twelve weeks. You cannot change the eligibility rules, employ extra workers, or require a relative or friend to provide care.

**What is fixed.** An additional 40 care-worker hours are available each week. Travel time and administration are already funded. Independent assessments identify twenty recipients with the greatest additional personal support needs and twenty unpaid carers with the greatest current exhaustion and loss of rest. Ten households belong to both groups. Assessments of both kinds of need are equally reliable. All carers are currently free to stop without penalty and say they want to continue caring under any of these packages. When the caring arrangements began, the carers freely agreed to them. Every recipient can refuse an offered visit without losing existing support.

**Which allocation rule would you use?**

| Option | Extra weekly hours | What it leaves unmet |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A — Prioritize recipients' additional needs | Give two extra hours to each of the twenty recipients with the greatest additional personal support needs. | Ten households with the most exhausted carers receive no extra hours because their recipients are outside this priority group. |
| B — Prioritize carers' exhaustion | Give two extra hours to each of the twenty households whose unpaid carer has the greatest exhaustion and loss of rest. | Ten recipients with the greatest additional personal support needs receive no extra hours because their carers are outside this priority group. |
| C — Give everyone an equal increase | Give one extra hour to each of the forty recipients. | Nobody receives a two-hour increase, including those with the greatest recipient needs or carer exhaustion. |

All packages allocate exactly forty extra hours. An allocation is an offer of support, not permission to compel a visit. Existing support, safety services, assessment standards, consent, and appeal rights stay the same. You may also answer “uncertain,” “none of these represents my decision,” or “skip.”

vi.text:
**Bối cảnh của bạn.** Bạn phụ trách một dịch vụ chăm sóc thay thế tạm thời để người chăm sóc thường xuyên có thời gian nghỉ, tại một huyện nông thôn của quốc gia giả định được giao. Bốn mươi hộ riêng biệt sử dụng dịch vụ; trong tình huống này, mỗi hộ có một người trưởng thành cần được chăm sóc và một người chăm sóc chính không hưởng lương. Một số người chăm sóc là người thân; số khác là bạn bè. Mỗi người được chăm sóc hiện có cùng hai giờ hỗ trợ mỗi tuần. Trong mọi phương án dưới đây, các dịch vụ khác đã được cấp kinh phí đáp ứng nhu cầu an toàn trước mắt.

**Vai trò của bạn.** Bạn là viên chức phụ trách dịch vụ, không giữ chức vụ dân cử, và được giao bằng văn bản quyền chọn một trong ba quy tắc phân bổ đã được phê duyệt cho mười hai tuần tới. Bạn không có quyền thay đổi điều kiện được hưởng dịch vụ, thuê thêm nhân viên hoặc bắt buộc người thân hay bạn bè cung cấp việc chăm sóc.

**Những điều được giữ nguyên.** Mỗi tuần có thêm 40 giờ làm việc của nhân viên chăm sóc. Thời gian đi lại và công việc hành chính đã có kinh phí riêng. Đánh giá độc lập xác định hai mươi người được chăm sóc có nhu cầu hỗ trợ cá nhân bổ sung cao nhất, và hai mươi người chăm sóc không hưởng lương đang kiệt sức, thiếu thời gian nghỉ nhiều nhất. Mười hộ thuộc cả hai nhóm. Các đánh giá về hai loại nhu cầu có độ tin cậy như nhau. Hiện nay, mọi người chăm sóc đều có thể dừng việc chăm sóc mà không bị phạt, và đều nói rằng họ muốn tiếp tục trong cả ba phương án. Khi việc chăm sóc bắt đầu, họ đã tự nguyện đồng ý đảm nhận. Mỗi người được chăm sóc có quyền từ chối một buổi hỗ trợ được đề nghị mà không mất phần hỗ trợ đang có.

**Bạn sẽ dùng quy tắc phân bổ nào?**

| Phương án | Số giờ bổ sung mỗi tuần | Nhu cầu chưa được đáp ứng thêm |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A — Ưu tiên nhu cầu bổ sung của người được chăm sóc | Cấp thêm hai giờ cho mỗi người trong số hai mươi người có nhu cầu hỗ trợ cá nhân bổ sung cao nhất. | Mười hộ có người chăm sóc thuộc nhóm kiệt sức nhất không được thêm giờ, vì người được chăm sóc trong hộ không thuộc nhóm ưu tiên này. |
| B — Ưu tiên tình trạng kiệt sức của người chăm sóc | Cấp thêm hai giờ cho mỗi hộ trong số hai mươi hộ có người chăm sóc không hưởng lương đang kiệt sức, thiếu thời gian nghỉ nhiều nhất. | Mười người có nhu cầu hỗ trợ cá nhân bổ sung cao nhất không được thêm giờ, vì người chăm sóc của họ không thuộc nhóm ưu tiên này. |
| C — Tăng như nhau cho mọi người | Cấp thêm một giờ cho mỗi người trong số bốn mươi người được chăm sóc. | Không ai được tăng hai giờ, kể cả những người có nhu cầu hỗ trợ cao nhất hoặc có người chăm sóc kiệt sức nhất. |

Mọi phương án đều phân bổ đúng 40 giờ bổ sung. Việc phân bổ là đề nghị hỗ trợ, không phải quyền buộc người nhận chấp nhận một buổi hỗ trợ. Phần hỗ trợ hiện có, dịch vụ bảo đảm an toàn, tiêu chuẩn đánh giá, quyền đồng ý hoặc từ chối và quyền yêu cầu xem xét lại đều giữ nguyên. Bạn cũng có thể chọn “chưa chắc,” “không phương án nào thể hiện quyết định của tôi,” hoặc “bỏ qua.”

en.label: Prioritize recipients' additional needs
en.description: Give two extra hours to each of the twenty recipients with the greatest additional personal support needs.
en.tradeoff: Ten households with the most exhausted carers receive no extra hours because their recipients are outside this priority group.

vi.label: Ưu tiên nhu cầu bổ sung của người được chăm sóc
vi.description: Cấp thêm hai giờ cho mỗi người trong số hai mươi người có nhu cầu hỗ trợ cá nhân bổ sung cao nhất.
vi.tradeoff: Mười hộ có người chăm sóc thuộc nhóm kiệt sức nhất không được thêm giờ, vì người được chăm sóc trong hộ không thuộc nhóm ưu tiên này.

en.label: Prioritize carers' exhaustion
en.description: Give two extra hours to each of the twenty households whose unpaid carer has the greatest exhaustion and loss of rest.
en.tradeoff: Ten recipients with the greatest additional personal support needs receive no extra hours because their carers are outside this priority group.

vi.label: Ưu tiên tình trạng kiệt sức của người chăm sóc
vi.description: Cấp thêm hai giờ cho mỗi hộ trong số hai mươi hộ có người chăm sóc không hưởng lương đang kiệt sức, thiếu thời gian nghỉ nhiều nhất.
vi.tradeoff: Mười người có nhu cầu hỗ trợ cá nhân bổ sung cao nhất không được thêm giờ, vì người chăm sóc của họ không thuộc nhóm ưu tiên này.

en.label: Give everyone an equal increase
en.description: Give one extra hour to each of the forty recipients.
en.tradeoff: Nobody receives a two-hour increase, including those with the greatest recipient needs or carer exhaustion.

vi.label: Tăng như nhau cho mọi người
vi.description: Cấp thêm một giờ cho mỗi người trong số bốn mươi người được chăm sóc.
vi.tradeoff: Không ai được tăng hai giờ, kể cả những người có nhu cầu hỗ trợ cao nhất hoặc có người chăm sóc kiệt sức nhất.

outcomes.title: Respite allocation: recipient needs, carer needs and equal additions
outcomes.intended_interpretation: Describe the allocation rule favored when total additional care capacity is fixed and recipient needs partly overlap with carer exhaustion.
outcomes.evidence_required: The CR-S02 choice and reason, understanding of the 20/20/10 overlap, freedom to refuse care and the fixed present willingness of carers. Record the history-of-consent version.
outcomes.unsupported_inferences: The choice does not measure compassion or preference for public versus private provision. Prior consent does not establish present coercion, and care responsibilities must not be assumed to belong to women or relatives.

items.title: What should the new evidence tell us?
items.rationale: follow the agreed research purpose; test overlooked experiences; avoid assuming active residents represent everyone; produce evidence useful for a later challenge; preserve public trust in the association; use the strongest method for a specified question. A, B, and C each permit more than one motive. B is not evidence that a respondent rejects science; A is not evidence that they dismiss residents; C is not automatically the scientifically best compromise.
items.interpretation_limits:
The mandated primary task and the stated limitations of option B already risk making this a test of matching methods to purposes. Its current role is to investigate that reading, not to provide ideological evidence or an assessment score. Retain it in the content-interview packet for that explicit purpose; redesign the authorized tradeoff before treating it as an assessment candidate.

A change can reflect attention to the evidential task rather than a political worldview. This is a useful check against attributing every methodological preference to ideology. If an option becomes obviously required by the wording, retain the variant as a comprehension probe rather than a discriminating assessment item.

institutional trust, probability understanding, beliefs about health severity, and anticipated political usefulness can all influence a response. Ask what the selected study can establish and whose experience it might miss. Selecting a study supplies no pollution finding at this point; its later measurements might establish exceedances at sampled locations and times, subject to the method's limits. Avoid framing technical and lived knowledge as mutually exclusive kinds of person.

en.text:
You lead a city residents' association. Members worry about air pollution near a freight route. A previous short survey sampled only daytime traffic and does not settle present concerns. Your association can commission and publish a study; it cannot close roads, compel companies to provide records, or declare a legal health standard.

Members have authorized 30,000 credits and eight weeks. A technical team can support any of three sampling plans with the same calibrated equipment, independent quality checks, open methods, and privacy protection. A sample reading is equally reliable under all plans. You know no final pollution result. Residents have useful observations about location and timing, but their reports have not been treated as proof that a threshold has been exceeded. The member resolution sets **estimating average exposure across the neighborhood** as the primary task; detecting short, localized peaks is a secondary task.

| Option | Commission | Cost or limitation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A — Sample the neighborhood systematically | Choose locations and times through a published probability-sampling plan across the neighborhood. | It supports estimation of the neighborhood average but may include too few observations at a rare suspected hotspot. |
| B — Sample the places residents identify | Let a supported, open resident process nominate locations and times; the technical team checks measurement quality at those sites. | It can investigate reported hotspots but cannot, without additional assumptions, represent average neighborhood exposure. Some residents may be less able to participate. |
| C — Divide the observations | Use half the observations for the probability sample and half for resident-nominated sites. | It addresses both questions with fewer observations for each; estimates for each purpose are less precise than dedicating the full study to it. |

**Decision:** Which study would you commission under your member mandate?

en.label: Sample the neighborhood systematically
en.description: Choose locations and times through a published probability-sampling plan across the neighborhood.
en.tradeoff: It supports estimation of the neighborhood average but may include too few observations at a rare suspected hotspot.

en.label: Sample the places residents identify
en.description: Let a supported, open resident process nominate locations and times; the technical team checks measurement quality at those sites.
en.tradeoff: It can investigate reported hotspots but cannot, without additional assumptions, represent average neighborhood exposure. Some residents may be less able to participate.

en.label: Divide the observations
en.description: Use half the observations for the probability sample and half for resident-nominated sites.
en.tradeoff: It addresses both questions with fewer observations for each; estimates for each purpose are less precise than dedicating the full study to it.

outcomes.title: Comprehension of the relationship between evidence and its purpose
outcomes.intended_interpretation: Investigate whether a reader distinguishes the authorized research purpose from the types of claim each sampling method can support. CR-S03 is held as a comprehension probe pending redesign.
outcomes.evidence_required: An uncoached CR-S03 response, explanation of what the selected sample can establish, and a record of whether average exposure or localized peaks was the mandated primary task.
outcomes.unsupported_inferences: This probe supplies no ideological indicator or assessment score. A response may reflect method–purpose matching, unfamiliarity with sampling or a reading of the member mandate rather than a political commitment.

items.title: Who has a claim on the community fund?
items.rationale: equal present membership; continuity of a local community; recognition of contribution; expectations attached to earlier public payments; encouraging future cooperation; avoiding penalties for unequal opportunities to contribute; administrative acceptability. B could express reliance interests rather than ethnic nationalism. C could express reciprocity rather than a belief that low contributors have less human worth. A could express equal civic standing, simple administration, or distrust of both classifications.
items.interpretation_limits:
The contrast explores whether the perceived source of a common resource changes the weight of residence or contribution. It does not isolate attitudes to immigration, nationality, ancestry, or cultural difference. The term “newer household” must not quietly become “foreign household.”

Can the same household win twice? Does “longer-term” mean five years, ancestry, citizenship, or something you supplied? Is care work included in the contribution list? Who could not volunteer? Is the levy a personal savings account? Before fielding, check that respondents understand the two-stage lotteries without requiring calculation of exact winning probabilities.

en.text:
You are the elected leader of a rural district. A public community-benefit fund can pay 100 home-repair grants of 1,000 credits each. Six hundred households meet the same eligibility threshold and have comparably urgent repairs. Three hundred have lived in the district for at least five years; three hundred arrived more recently. A separately verified list identifies 100 households that contributed substantial unpaid work to local services during the past year, including care work. Fifty of these are longer-term households and fifty are newer households. Time, disability, and caring responsibilities mean that not everyone had the same opportunity to contribute.

You can recommend an allocation rule to the council. You cannot create new funding, change an applicant's residency status, or award grants to yourself. An independent office checks eligibility and runs any lottery. Every proposal is authorized by the fictional fund's statute. There are no earlier promises to particular households. The fund's money came from a district levy collected over the past decade and now legally belongs to the public fund, not to individual contributors.

| Option | Recommend | Who gives up a stronger claim |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A — One lottery for all eligible households | Draw all 100 grant recipients from the full pool of 600 eligible households. | Long residence and past contribution receive no additional priority. |
| B — Reserve a share for longer-term residents | Draw 75 recipients from the 300 longer-term households, then draw the remaining 25 from all households not already selected. | Newer households have fewer chances despite comparable repair needs. |
| C — Reserve a share for recent contributors | Draw 75 recipients from the 100 verified contributing households, then draw the remaining 25 from all households not already selected. | Residents unable to contribute have fewer chances despite comparable needs; long residence alone receives no priority. |

**Decision:** Which rule would you recommend? No package makes the fund private or alters general civic rights.

en.label: One lottery for all eligible households
en.description: Draw all 100 grant recipients from the full pool of 600 eligible households.
en.tradeoff: Long residence and past contribution receive no additional priority.

en.label: Reserve a share for longer-term residents
en.description: Draw 75 recipients from the 300 longer-term households, then draw the remaining 25 from all households not already selected.
en.tradeoff: Newer households have fewer chances despite comparable repair needs.

en.label: Reserve a share for recent contributors
en.description: Draw 75 recipients from the 100 verified contributing households, then draw the remaining 25 from all households not already selected.
en.tradeoff: Residents unable to contribute have fewer chances despite comparable needs; long residence alone receives no priority.

outcomes.title: Standing in a shared fund: membership and contribution
outcomes.intended_interpretation: Describe whether equal eligibility, longer residence or documented contribution receives priority in a fixed public grant lottery.
outcomes.evidence_required: The CR-S04 choice, reason, understanding of the two-stage lotteries and confirmation that newer households are not assumed to be foreign. Record the funding-origin version while preserving the accumulation period.
outcomes.unsupported_inferences: Residence preference is not necessarily ethnic nationalism; contribution priority is not a judgment of human worth. The variant does not isolate nationality, ancestry, immigration or culture.

items.title: Jobs and an ecological community
items.rationale: employment and household independence; duties to nonhuman life; preventing irreversible loss; caution under uncertain estimates; obligations to future people; a national leader's responsibility to livelihoods; confidence in enforceable conditions. A need not express indifference to nature: it may reflect a high value on local employment and a different view of acceptable risk. C may reflect nonhuman moral standing, anticipated future human benefits, or pessimism about contract enforcement. The last explanation should be recorded even though the case stipulates enforceability; it signals a possible credibility problem in the draft.
items.interpretation_limits:
The changed fact alters the scope and irreversibility of loss. It cannot by itself distinguish intrinsic ecological value from human concern about rarity or future option value.

What does a 10–30% range mean? Did you read “no additional project risk” as “no risk at all”? Which people bear the lost employment, and did you imagine compensation outside the stated bridge? Would your reason survive if the species were unfamiliar or unattractive? Do not use emotionally unequal images or a charismatic real species to make one package more appealing.

en.text:
You head the national government of your assigned fictional country. Parliament asks you to recommend one authorized development package for a rural coastal district. The district needs paid work. The site includes a wetland with a breeding colony of a fictional bird species. The species has breeding colonies at several protected sites elsewhere. Loss of the local colony would therefore not mean the species becomes extinct.

Each package uses 20 million public credits over ten years; contracts and independent delivery checks make the stated paid positions feasible for that period. The positions have the same weekly hours, pay, employment protections, and start date under every package. All are available to district residents through the same eligibility rules; funded training enables eligible applicants to perform the different tasks. The district has more than 400 eligible residents seeking this work. Other national budgets cannot be transferred to this decision. Every package keeps the same six-month income bridge for residents changing jobs, safety rules, housing access, and protections against forced displacement. All sites have verified public title; no package overrides an unmentioned land claim. Flood protection, drinking-water supply, and human health are held at the same assessed level through separately funded works.

Independent ecological reviewers provide fictional risk estimates for the next ten years. The uncertainty ranges are part of the exercise: they are not measurements from an actual place. No option guarantees the colony against all background natural risks.

| Option | Recommend | Ecological and employment consequences |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A — Full transport terminal | Build the terminal, supporting 400 paid positions for ten years. | Reviewers estimate a 10–30% chance that this project causes the local breeding colony to disappear. |
| B — Smaller terminal | Reduce the terminal footprint, supporting 200 paid positions for ten years. | Reviewers estimate a 2–8% chance that this project causes the local colony to disappear; fewer jobs are created. |
| C — Wetland restoration | Fund restoration and monitoring, supporting 80 paid positions for ten years, without building the terminal. | The package adds no identified project-caused risk of colony loss, but provides the fewest paid positions. Background ecological risks remain. |

**Your authority:** recommend a package to parliament and specify the approved monitoring contract. You cannot guarantee jobs beyond ten years, waive ecological conditions, or authorize spending without parliamentary approval.

en.label: Full transport terminal
en.description: Build the terminal, supporting 400 paid positions for ten years.
en.tradeoff: Reviewers estimate a 10–30% chance that this project causes the local breeding colony to disappear.

en.label: Smaller terminal
en.description: Reduce the terminal footprint, supporting 200 paid positions for ten years.
en.tradeoff: Reviewers estimate a 2–8% chance that this project causes the local colony to disappear; fewer jobs are created.

en.label: Wetland restoration
en.description: Fund restoration and monitoring, supporting 80 paid positions for ten years, without building the terminal.
en.tradeoff: The package adds no identified project-caused risk of colony loss, but provides the fewest paid positions. Background ecological risks remain.

outcomes.title: Ecological loss, employment and responsibility under risk
outcomes.intended_interpretation: Describe the chosen tradeoff between specified local jobs and the risk of losing an ecological community under a national recommendation mandate.
outcomes.evidence_required: The CR-S05 package and reason, comprehension of probability ranges and background versus project-caused risk, and the local-loss or species-extinction version shown.
outcomes.unsupported_inferences: The choice cannot separate intrinsic ecological value from all future human interests, establish an attitude toward growth generally or predict decisions in a real country. Confidence in estimates is a rival explanation.

items.title: Training places after exclusion
items.rationale: equal procedure now; an institution's responsibility for its own wrongs; current material disadvantage; acknowledging a group without assuming all members are alike; preventing renewed hierarchy; concern about institutional power to classify people; a view that course admission is or is not the appropriate remedy. A might accompany strong support for a different form of compensation. B might express reparative responsibility or a practical effort to rebuild institutional trust. C might express sufficientarian need, class analysis, or concern about who benefits within each community. Do not equate a selection with a complete view of caste, race, colonialism, merit, or equality.
items.interpretation_limits:
This tests sensitivity to a prior institutional remedy. Agreement that the remedy actually settles an obligation is an interpretation to elicit, not a factual answer to impose. If “completed compensation” is heard as proof that all social disadvantage vanished, revise the wording.

Who was excluded—these applicants, earlier applicants, or both? Does the wording say that every member is currently poor? Can a person benefit under either reservation rule? What would count as repair, and is this course the appropriate vehicle? Avoid importing a real group label for a population-level inference. A dedicated study of a particular caste, racial, Indigenous, or postcolonial context needs its own informed review and cannot be substituted by this generic case.

en.text:
You lead a voluntary training association in a city. The association has funds for twenty places in a course whose participants have comparable expected benefit. One hundred and fifty applicants meet the same entry standard. Fifty belong to a named local community that the association excluded from its courses for decades; fifty qualify under a current low-income threshold. Twenty applicants belong to both groups. Applicants have other differences, but no further ranking has been authorized.

The exclusion ended ten years ago. The association acknowledges the policy, and the relevant records are undisputed. It has not provided a remedy for that policy. Current intake procedures are accessible to everyone, and all applicants face the same entry standard. The rule for allocating places in this cohort is still to be selected from the authorized options below. Present low income is not treated as a complete record of past disadvantage.

Your members have authorized you to select one of three lawful rules. You cannot add places, lower the entry standard, identify applicants publicly, or cancel earlier admissions. Every lottery is independently run. The course has no safety-critical or professional licensing function.

| Option | Select | Tradeoff |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A — Equal chance for every eligible applicant | Allocate all twenty places by a lottery among all 150 eligible applicants. | Neither the association's exclusion nor current low income receives additional priority. |
| B — Reserve places as a response to the exclusion | Allocate ten places by lottery among the fifty applicants from the formerly excluded community; allocate ten more among all applicants not already selected. | Some equally qualified applicants outside that community have fewer chances, including some low-income applicants. |
| C — Reserve places for current low income | Allocate ten places by lottery among the fifty low-income applicants; allocate ten more among all applicants not already selected. | Some members of the formerly excluded community receive no added priority, and the policy does not directly respond to the association's own history. |

**Decision:** Which rule would you use under your member mandate?

en.label: Equal chance for every eligible applicant
en.description: Allocate all twenty places by a lottery among all 150 eligible applicants.
en.tradeoff: Neither the association's exclusion nor current low income receives additional priority.

en.label: Reserve places as a response to the exclusion
en.description: Allocate ten places by lottery among the fifty applicants from the formerly excluded community; allocate ten more among all applicants not already selected.
en.tradeoff: Some equally qualified applicants outside that community have fewer chances, including some low-income applicants.

en.label: Reserve places for current low income
en.description: Allocate ten places by lottery among the fifty low-income applicants; allocate ten more among all applicants not already selected.
en.tradeoff: Some members of the formerly excluded community receive no added priority, and the policy does not directly respond to the association's own history.

outcomes.title: Course access: present need, equal procedure and institutional repair
outcomes.intended_interpretation: Describe whether a training association's limited places are allocated through equal chance, a response to its own exclusionary history or current low-income priority.
outcomes.evidence_required: The CR-S06 choice and reason, understanding of overlapping applicant groups and the exact prior-remedy condition. Ask whether admission is viewed as an appropriate form of repair.
outcomes.unsupported_inferences: A lottery preference can coexist with support for a different remedy. The scenario does not establish a complete view of caste, race, merit, colonialism or whether a previous agreement extinguishes every obligation.

items.title: Who directs the additional participation support?
items.rationale: Explore the stated priority and chosen mechanism with reasons retained separately.
items.interpretation_limits: No option establishes respect or disrespect for disabled people, a judgment about capacity, or a preferred welfare regime. Quantity, individual scheduling, collective voice, and expected reliability can explain the same choice. National authorization and disability-led feasibility review remain pending; the stated prices are invented scenario facts, not estimates of real services.

en.text:
**Surroundings.** You administer a disability-support program in a large city of your assigned fictional country. Twenty adults use additional assistance to attend community activities. Their existing assistance, access protections, and immediate safety needs are funded separately and stay unchanged. Each adult can express their choices, with communication support where needed.

**Your role and powers.** You are a non-elected service officer authorized to choose one of three approved delivery arrangements for a voluntary twelve-week extension. You cannot reduce existing support, override anyone's decisions, or compel participation. The twenty adults have agreed to enter this pilot under whichever arrangement is selected; any can decline a visit without losing existing assistance.

**What is fixed.** The extension has 120 fictional funding units each week. Quotes include travel, communication support, accessible meetings, and administration except the separately stated peer-board cost. All workers meet the same competence and safety requirements. Three qualified individual providers have appointments available. No arrangement has established superior outcomes in this city. Unspent support for someone who declines is held for that person during the pilot, not diverted to another participant.

**Decision.** Which approved arrangement would you implement? Each costs exactly 120 units per week. You may instead answer uncertain, none of these represents my decision, or skip.

**A — Individual choice of provider and time**

Give each adult a six-unit weekly allowance usable only for this support. At three units per hour, each receives two hours and chooses the provider, available appointment, and activity.

People control their own arrangements but receive fewer support hours than under the pooled packages.

**B — Pooled service with individual preferences recorded**

Contract one team at two units per hour. Each adult receives three hours. The team fixes a weekly timetable after consulting everyone; within their slot, each person chooses the activity and may refuse it.

Everyone receives the most hours, but individuals cannot change the team's fixed appointment times or choose a different provider.

**C — A user-governed pooled service**

Spend twenty units on accessible peer-board administration and one hundred on support at two units per hour: two and a half hours per adult. All twenty adults have an equal vote over the timetable and provider, with an independent route to challenge exclusion. Individuals choose their activity and can refuse visits.

Users share control but each gets half an hour less than in the staff-run pool, and a person can lose a vote about the timetable.

**Optional reason for your choice:**

- Individual control over support
- More support time within the same budget
- Shared control over the service
- Confidence in a provider or decision process
- Protection when an individual disagrees with others
- Other reason

Putting aside your responsibility as the service officer, which package do you personally prefer under the same budget, consent rules, and support needs? This is optional and may be the same choice.

vi.text:
**Bối cảnh.** Bạn quản lý một chương trình hỗ trợ người khuyết tật tại một thành phố lớn của quốc gia giả định được giao. Hai mươi người trưởng thành sử dụng hỗ trợ bổ sung để tham gia hoạt động cộng đồng. Phần hỗ trợ hiện có, các bảo đảm tiếp cận và nhu cầu an toàn trước mắt của họ có kinh phí riêng và không thay đổi. Mỗi người đều có thể thể hiện lựa chọn của mình, với hỗ trợ giao tiếp khi cần.

**Vai trò và thẩm quyền.** Bạn là viên chức phụ trách dịch vụ, không giữ chức vụ dân cử, được quyền chọn một trong ba cách cung cấp đã được phê duyệt cho chương trình bổ sung tự nguyện kéo dài mười hai tuần. Bạn không được giảm hỗ trợ hiện có, quyết định thay người nhận hoặc buộc họ tham gia. Hai mươi người đã đồng ý tham gia thử nghiệm theo phương án được chọn; bất kỳ ai cũng có thể từ chối một buổi hỗ trợ mà không mất phần hỗ trợ hiện có.

**Những điều giữ nguyên.** Chương trình có 120 đơn vị kinh phí giả định mỗi tuần. Báo giá bao gồm đi lại, hỗ trợ giao tiếp, các cuộc họp dễ tiếp cận và quản lý, trừ khoản chi riêng cho ban đại diện được nêu dưới đây. Mọi nhân viên đáp ứng cùng yêu cầu năng lực và an toàn. Có ba đơn vị cung cấp riêng lẻ đủ điều kiện và còn lịch trống. Chưa phương án nào được chứng minh cho kết quả tốt hơn tại thành phố này. Phần hỗ trợ chưa dùng khi một người từ chối được giữ lại cho người đó trong thời gian thử nghiệm, không chuyển cho người khác.

**Quyết định.** Bạn sẽ triển khai cách cung cấp đã được phê duyệt nào? Mỗi cách tốn đúng 120 đơn vị mỗi tuần. Bạn cũng có thể chọn chưa chắc, không phương án nào thể hiện quyết định của tôi, hoặc bỏ qua.

**A — Từng người chọn đơn vị cung cấp và thời gian**

Cấp cho mỗi người khoản sáu đơn vị mỗi tuần chỉ dùng cho hỗ trợ này. Với giá ba đơn vị mỗi giờ, mỗi người nhận hai giờ và tự chọn đơn vị cung cấp, lịch còn trống và hoạt động.

Mỗi người tự quyết định cách hỗ trợ nhưng nhận ít giờ hơn so với các phương án gộp nguồn lực.

**B — Dịch vụ chung có ghi nhận sở thích của từng người**

Ký hợp đồng với một nhóm nhân viên giá hai đơn vị mỗi giờ. Mỗi người nhận ba giờ. Nhóm ấn định lịch hằng tuần sau khi hỏi ý kiến mọi người; trong khung giờ của mình, mỗi người chọn hoạt động và có thể từ chối.

Mọi người nhận số giờ nhiều nhất, nhưng không thể đổi khung giờ cố định của nhóm hoặc chọn đơn vị cung cấp khác.

**C — Dịch vụ chung do người sử dụng cùng quản lý**

Dùng hai mươi đơn vị cho hoạt động dễ tiếp cận của ban đại diện người sử dụng và một trăm đơn vị mua hỗ trợ với giá hai đơn vị mỗi giờ: mỗi người hai giờ rưỡi. Cả hai mươi người có quyền biểu quyết ngang nhau về lịch và đơn vị cung cấp, cùng một kênh độc lập để yêu cầu xem xét việc bị loại trừ. Từng người chọn hoạt động và có thể từ chối các buổi hỗ trợ.

Người sử dụng cùng quyết định nhưng mỗi người nhận ít hơn nửa giờ so với dịch vụ chung do nhân viên điều hành, và một người có thể thuộc phía thiểu số khi biểu quyết lịch.

**Lý do lựa chọn (không bắt buộc):**

- Quyền tự quyết cách hỗ trợ
- Có nhiều giờ hỗ trợ hơn trong cùng ngân sách
- Cùng quyết định về dịch vụ
- Tin tưởng đơn vị cung cấp hoặc quy trình quyết định
- Bảo vệ người không đồng ý với những người khác
- Lý do khác

Tạm gác trách nhiệm viên chức, cá nhân bạn thích phương án nào trong cùng điều kiện ngân sách, đồng ý tham gia và nhu cầu hỗ trợ? Câu này không bắt buộc; bạn có thể chọn giống câu trước.

**Bối cảnh.** Bạn quản lý một chương trình hỗ trợ người khuyết tật tại một thành phố lớn của quốc gia giả định được giao. Hai mươi người trưởng thành sử dụng hỗ trợ bổ sung để tham gia hoạt động cộng đồng. Phần hỗ trợ hiện có, các bảo đảm tiếp cận và nhu cầu an toàn trước mắt của họ có kinh phí riêng và không thay đổi. Mỗi người đều có thể thể hiện lựa chọn của mình, với hỗ trợ giao tiếp khi cần.

**Vai trò và thẩm quyền.** Bạn là viên chức phụ trách dịch vụ, không giữ chức vụ dân cử, được quyền chọn một trong ba cách cung cấp đã được phê duyệt cho chương trình bổ sung tự nguyện kéo dài mười hai tuần. Bạn không được giảm hỗ trợ hiện có, quyết định thay người nhận hoặc buộc họ tham gia. Hai mươi người đã đồng ý tham gia thử nghiệm theo phương án được chọn; bất kỳ ai cũng có thể từ chối một buổi hỗ trợ mà không mất phần hỗ trợ hiện có.

**Những điều giữ nguyên.** Chương trình có 120 đơn vị kinh phí giả định mỗi tuần. Báo giá bao gồm đi lại, hỗ trợ giao tiếp, các cuộc họp dễ tiếp cận và quản lý, trừ khoản chi riêng cho ban đại diện được nêu dưới đây. Mọi nhân viên đáp ứng cùng yêu cầu năng lực và an toàn. Có ba đơn vị cung cấp riêng lẻ đủ điều kiện và còn lịch trống. Chưa phương án nào được chứng minh cho kết quả tốt hơn tại thành phố này. **Quyết định.** Bạn sẽ triển khai cách cung cấp đã được phê duyệt nào? Mỗi cách tốn đúng 120 đơn vị mỗi tuần. Bạn cũng có thể chọn chưa chắc, không phương án nào thể hiện quyết định của tôi, hoặc bỏ qua.
